answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it earns, like a walnut that only opens after real work cracks it. Reputation then acts as a lantern: peers publicly vouch for agents whose past work checks out, so newcomers start dim and must earn light over time. Random audits — a juniper-like prickly check, cheap to run but painful to fake — sample agents and slash deposits when behavior does not match claims, making mass fake identities unprofitable.
